chunks: From al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Uthman al-Halabi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:

A man from the Mawali of Banu Marwan deposited a thousand dinars with me, then he disappeared, and I did not know what to do with the dinars. So I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and mentioned that to him, saying, 'You are more entitled to them.' He said, 'No, indeed my father (peace be upon him) used to say: We are among them in the status of a truce; we return their trusts, restore their lost property, and establish testimony for them and against them. When the factions diverge, no one will have the capacity to remain.'
ai.seo_question: What is the status of deposited wealth when the owner is unknown according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that deposited wealth remains the property of the depositor, rejecting the notion of escheat to the Imam, while establishing the doctrine of 'hudnah' (temporary coexistence) with the ruling authorities. This period of stability involves fulfilling public duties such as returning trusts and testifying in court, which will conclude when political factions diverge, marking the transition to the Imam's hidden or final presence. This hadith underscores the pragmatic political stance of the Imams during the Umayyad and Abbasid eras, balancing religious integrity with social engagement.
